newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - April 15.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

-- CAMAS AND BARDON LINK IN 540 MILLION POUND MERGER Building materials groups Camas and Bardon yesterday announced an all-paper merger to create Britain's fifth-largest aggregates business, Aggregate Industries. Camas' base in the southwest will combine with Bardon's Midlands and northern operations and unifying operations in the USA.

-- AB FOODS TARGETS ACQUISITION WITH 1.5 BILLION POUND CASH PILE Associated British Foods yesterday ruled out a share buyback, saying they hoped to use their projected cash funds of 1.5 billion pounds stg to make a major acquisition instead. The group revealed a rise of only 2 percent in interim pre-tax profits to 201 million pounds stg as it was hit by the strength of sterling and a fall in investment income.

-- GUS BUYS US DIRECTING MARKETING FIRM Great Universal Stores moved further away from mail order and closer to information services with its purchase of Direct Marketing Technology of the USA for up to 180 million pounds stg. The company exists to analyse and market data on the spending patterns of American consumers and related strategies.

-- CO-OP 6 BILLION POUND MERGER PROPOSAL REJECTED The Co-operative Retail Society has rejected a merger proposal to combine the various parts of the Co-operative movement into a 6 billion pound stg retail giant. The proposal came from Graham Melmouth, chief executive of the Co-operative Wholesale Society, who announced a 21 percent fall in trading profits at CWS to 41.5 million pounds in 1996. The organization faces takeover pressure from Andrew Regan of Lancia Trust.

-- GLAXO ATTACKED OVER US POLITICAL DONATIONS Glaxo Wellcome is to come under attack from shareholders for giving US$500,000 dollars to US political parties without disclosing this in its report and accounts. The company gave up giving donations to UK political parties two years ago. It admitted the US donations, mostly to the Republican party, in response to a letter from Pirc, the corporate governance consultants.

-- HANSON PLANS SALE OF ELECTRICAL DIVISION Hanson, the former conglomerate that completed a four-part demerger in February, announced plans to sell its electrical division to management for 135 million pounds stg. The deal is backed by venture capital house Cinven. The deal leaves Hanson trading only in building materials and distributing cranes.

-- TORY DOLE FIGURES 'FLAWED' A report to be released today from the Employment Policy Institute contradicts Conservative party claims that falling unemployment is cutting into Britain's workless families, calling it 'flawed'. The report shows that, while the official jobless count has fallen more than 1 million, the proportion of households without a single wage earner has risen to almost one in five.

-- NATWEST STAFF LEADER SEEKS ELECTION TO BOARD Rory Murphy, general secretary of the NatWest Staff Association, is to seek election to the bank's board of directors. Murphy is seeking election in order to protect the bank's profit-related pay scheme from the recent 900 million pound stg derivatives losses at NatWest Markets.

-- VIRGIN NAMES SOUTH AFRICAN PARTNERS IN SUN AIR BID Virgin Atlantic Airways, seeking to buy regional South African airline Sun Air for 28 million pounds stg, yesterday named a local consortium of business partners. They are members of a group called Bhekilanga, which includes the investment arm of the South African Railway and Harbour Workers' Union.

-- CHANCELLOR DINES ON A PERFECT COCKTAIL OF STATISTICS A week of key economic statistics began yesterday, with the news that factory gate inflation fell last month to the lowest in over 10 years. The strength of the pound contributed to the drop. Separate survey results showed that high street sales grew at a slower rate in March. The figures are good news for the Chancellor, and will be followed this week by further encouraging statistics. However, analysts warned of the danger of inflationary pressures because of the strength of the economy outside manufacturing.

-- BASE RATE FEARS FUELLED BY 6 BILLION POUND WINDFALL More than 6 billion pounds stg is set to pour into the economy over the next few months via building society windfalls. The bonanza is likely to boost consumer spending and increase pressure for an interest rate rise. Alliance & Leicester revealed that 27.5 percent of the shares being given away in next week's 2.3 billion pound stg flotation are being cashed immediately.

-- BT PLANNING 45 MILLION POUND STAKE IN PORTUGAL British Telecom yesterday announced plans to buy a stake in Portugal Telecom, a move that BT hopes will give it an entry into the rapidly-growing Brazilian telecoms market. It also appears to move BT closer to its desire to sever Telefonica of Spain from its partnership with AT&T. BT is today holding an extraordinary general meeting to seek approval of its proposed merger with MCI of the USA.
